decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom is a high-value system released in 2019 with a long sales and service life in a growing niche, so withdrawing it after so few years would make little sense.
Small volume chambers stay in demand for small-field and stereotactic dosimetry, though overlap with other detectors in the portfolio adds some risk of consolidation, as happened with Product B.
Standard clinical ionization chambers are a core product line tied to absolute dosimetry and accredited calibration services, so dropping them is very unlikely.
Relative dosimetry chambers are needed for the firm's water phantom scanning workflows and support system sales, which gives them lasting relevance.
Thimble chambers are established reference instruments with steady clinical demand and links to the calibration business.
